title: What Happens on a Game Drive
excerpt: The game drive is the heart of every safari. What happens on a drive, how long it lasts and how to make the most of it.
body:
A game drive is a drive through a park in a safari vehicle, looking for wildlife with a guide.

## Morning drive

Starting at sunrise, when animals are active and the light is soft. Often the best time for predators.

## Afternoon drive

From around 15:00–16:00 until sunset. Animals become active again as it cools down.

## Full-day drive

In large parks like the Serengeti, you may stay out all day with a picnic lunch, to reach distant areas.

## What the guide does

The guide reads tracks, listens to alarm calls of birds and monkeys, watches vultures and communicates with other guides.

## Tips

- Bring binoculars.
- Dress in layers: mornings are cold, middays hot.
- Ask questions. Guides love to explain.
- Have patience: sometimes waiting pays off.

## How many per day

Usually two drives per day, with rest at midday. See [a typical safari day](/blog/safari-day-schedule/).
